stories.title: Bitcoin traders bet $2.9 million on a jump above $82,000 as rally turns overbought
stories.summary: Traders placed a $2.9 million wager that bitcoin will jump rapidly above $82,000 after the token topped $80,000 and solana rose 8%. More than $220 million in short positions were liquidated in 24 hours, and some technical indicators now flag the rally as overbought. Analysts say the next pullback will be the real test of the move's strength.
stories.whyItMatters: Heavy short liquidations and large directional bets show leverage is building fast, raising the odds of a sharp reversal if sentiment turns.
whatToWatch: Whether bitcoin holds above $80,000 through the next pullback
Whether the $82,000 options bet pays off
Further liquidation data as leverage unwinds
questions: Is the rally driven by real demand or short covering?
How much of the move rests on leverage versus spot buying?

stories.title: Coinbase launches tokenized stocks on Base, using Chainlink price feeds
stories.summary: Coinbase has gone live with tokenized stock trading on its Base network, using Chainlink oracles to provide on-chain price data. The launch puts Coinbase among a growing group of crypto firms racing to bring traditional equities onto blockchain rails.
stories.whyItMatters: Tokenized equities blur the line between crypto and traditional markets, and how regulators respond will shape how far the trend can go.
whatToWatch: Which stocks are supported at launch and how the list expands
Regulatory reaction to equities trading on a public blockchain
Competing tokenized-stock offerings from other exchanges
questions: What legal structure makes these tokens equivalent to real shares?
Are they available to US retail users or only offshore?

stories.title: Bitcoin tops $80,000 for the first time since May
stories.summary: Bitcoin crossed $80,000 for the first time since May, extending a recovery from recent lows alongside broader gains in crypto markets.
stories.whyItMatters: The $80,000 level is a widely watched marker, and reclaiming it signals renewed risk appetite after months of weakness.
whatToWatch: Whether bitcoin holds above $80,000 or reverses
Follow-through in altcoins and ETF flows
questions: What is driving the recovery — spot demand, short covering, or macro factors?

stories.title: Ethereum proposal would cut issuance by 33,800 ETH but break every deployed Altair light client
stories.summary: A new Ethereum proposal would lower ETH issuance by about 33,800 ETH, but it would also break every currently deployed Altair-era light client. The proposal sets lower token issuance against a real compatibility cost for existing lightweight node software.
stories.whyItMatters: Issuance changes affect ETH's supply, while breaking light clients raises questions about how upgrades get rolled out without disrupting existing infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Whether the proposal advances through Ethereum's governance process
How light-client developers respond or plan upgrades
Any revised version that avoids breaking compatibility
questions: Who bears the cost of fixing broken light clients?
What is the timeline for a possible activation?

stories.title: Ledger patches Ethereum app bug that could let a signed transaction differ from what's shown
stories.summary: Ledger has fixed a bug in its Ethereum app that could have let a transaction shown on screen differ from the one actually signed. The flaw struck at the core trust assumption of hardware wallets: that what you see is what you sign.
stories.whyItMatters: Hardware wallets are a last line of defense against theft, so any gap between displayed and signed transactions is a serious security concern for ETH holders.
whatToWatch: Whether Ledger discloses if the bug was exploited before the patch
User uptake of the patched app version
questions: How long was the flaw present before it was found and fixed?

sources.title: Ledger patched an Ethereum app bug that could show one transaction and sign another

stories.title: Fidelity's crypto ETFs win approval to stake 100% of holdings
stories.summary: Fidelity has been granted the ability to stake the full amount of crypto held in its ETFs, rather than a partial share. The filing also spelled out risks tied to delays investors could face if they try to exit staked positions.
stories.whyItMatters: Staking lets ETF issuers earn extra yield on top of price exposure, but it adds liquidity risk that matters to investors who expect quick redemptions.
whatToWatch: How Fidelity discloses exit-delay terms to investors
Whether other issuers seek similar full-staking approval
questions: How long could redemption delays run under stress?
Does staking yield pass to shareholders or stay with Fidelity?

sources.title: Fidelity grants ETFs power to stake 100% of crypto while outlining exit delay risks

stories.title: Bitcoin and ether ETFs grew $23 billion last week, but only $2.6 billion was new money
stories.summary: US bitcoin and ether ETFs added about $23 billion in value over the past week, but only roughly $2.6 billion of that came from new investor inflows. The rest reflects price gains on assets the funds already held.
stories.whyItMatters: The gap between headline growth and real new money is a useful check against reading AUM jumps as a surge in fresh demand.
whatToWatch: Whether net inflows pick up in coming weeks
Any divergence between bitcoin and ether flow trends
questions: Is inflow demand slowing even as prices climb?

stories.title: US sanctions target Iran's crypto sector over $100 million in oil-linked payments
stories.summary: US authorities have taken action against parts of Iran's crypto sector, citing more than $100 million in payments linked to oil sales. The action aims to cut off crypto-based channels used to move sanctioned funds.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows regulators still treat crypto rails as a sanctions-evasion risk, which can drive stricter compliance requirements across exchanges.
whatToWatch: Whether specific exchanges or wallets are named or frozen
Follow-on enforcement against intermediaries
questions: Which platforms or entities facilitated these payments?

stories.title: Crypto industry PAC lists congressional allies it plans to back this cycle
stories.summary: A crypto-focused political advocacy group has detailed which US congressional candidates it intends to support this year. The announcement lands as bitcoin just posted its second-best week since early 2021, giving the industry stronger financial and political momentum.
stories.whyItMatters: Industry-funded political spending shapes which lawmakers write crypto rules, so knowing who's backed helps track upcoming policy fights.
whatToWatch: Total spending the group commits this cycle
Election outcomes for the named candidates
questions: How much money is behind this backing?
Which committees do these lawmakers sit on?

stories.title: BNB Chain activates Pasteur hard fork to tighten bridge security
stories.summary: BNB Chain has activated its Pasteur hard fork, a network upgrade meant to strengthen the security of its cross-chain bridges. Bridges have long been a common target for exploits across the industry.
stories.whyItMatters: Bridge hacks have cost the industry billions, so security upgrades on a major chain like BNB Chain close off a persistent attack surface.
whatToWatch: Whether the upgrade heads off any near-term exploit attempts
Validator and node operator adoption of the fork
questions: What specific vulnerabilities does Pasteur address?

stories.title: FalconX asks SEC to regulate single-stock perpetuals from DeFi as swaps
stories.summary: Trading firm FalconX has petitioned the SEC to bring single-stock perpetual futures offered through DeFi platforms under existing swap regulations. The request targets what FalconX views as a regulatory gap between decentralized and traditional derivatives markets.
stories.whyItMatters: How regulators classify DeFi derivatives will determine whether decentralized platforms face the same compliance load as traditional swap dealers.
whatToWatch: Whether the SEC responds to or acts on the petition
Reaction from DeFi platforms offering these products
questions: Which specific platforms or products would be affected?
Does the SEC have jurisdiction over DeFi protocols without a central operator?

stories.title: Cypher Tank pitch event returns to Lugano, expanding its bitcoin founder bets
stories.summary: The Cypher Tank pitch competition is returning to Lugano, continuing its focus on funding bitcoin-focused startup founders. The event builds on the program's earlier work backing early-stage bitcoin ventures.
stories.whyItMatters: Early-stage funding events show where investor attention and capital are flowing within the bitcoin ecosystem.
whatToWatch: Which startups win backing at this year's event
Total capital committed through the program
questions: What criteria does Cypher Tank use to pick founders?
